column1: # One row per ruled_n in 1..=244, ascending, tab-separated, four fields:
#   ruled_n      the RULED item number on wayfinder map pardosa-jn1.
#   disposition  SPEC-BEARING (the ruling lands in >= 1 numbered clause)
#                or MAP-GOVERNANCE (it governs the map, the ADR corpus, bd hygiene,
#                citation audits, or the clean-room transfer, and has no clause here).
#   clause_ids   semicolon-separated clause ids for SPEC-BEARING rows; "-" otherwise.
#   note         short note for SPEC-BEARING rows; for MAP-GOVERNANCE rows, the reason,

column4: note
Mechanism stated in pardosa's own terms; no compliance claim, obligation rests with the consumer.
Erasure scoped to the artefact a migration writes; the artefact read is the consumer's to dispose.
A migration holds exclusive access to what it writes, with a named failure when it does not; the rule is stated and the locking mechanism left unspecified.
Refusal posture: guarantees stop at the pardosa layer. Backend-split migration-manager half is layer-4/5 and lands in a later slice.
Single writer, many readers as the universal invariant, with the source read and the target exclusively written during a migration and the writer role passing at cutover.
Fresh identity at every generation boundary; no event or fiber identity crosses, so no consumer-held reference survives.
Migration manager is a module of the pardosa crate and enters the surface fixed at 1.0; its failure vocabulary is fixed with it. The three-published-crate half is layer-6 and lands in a later slice.
The writer fence is unconditional, with no setting that withdraws it.
Compare-and-set to claim, with the losing writer stopping rather than retrying, and every write carrying the epoch.
Exactly two generations, and a second concurrent migration refused under a name the caller acts on.
The pairing of ownership record and event data stated as a property: bound by a shared name, decidable without reading either. The file-backend extensions are layer-10 artefact material.
The ownership recursion terminates: the ownership record carries its own claim as its first content and nothing governs it from above.

Verdict discipline only: indeterminate never folds into death. NOTE for the vocabulary slice: the ruling labels the verdict THREE-VALUED but enumerates two variants; the variant set is jn1.29's to state, not stated here.
Ordered creation, the two orphan verdicts derived from it, and repair refused in both directions.
The transfer test, stated normatively. Assumption named: the ruling left the test's document status unruled, and the document admits no non-normative slot.
Stale-epoch rejection assigned to every adapter's write path, where the invariant binds.
Draws the boundary between this map and the clean-room transfer map by kind of question. It governs which map rules what, and has no clause in a library specification.
No writer opens where the exclusion mechanism is unavailable; readers unaffected. The condition is named distinctly from another owner holding the artefact.
An unreadable ownership record refuses the write under its own name, distinct from stale-epoch rejection, leaving the artefact unchanged and the events with the caller.
Both caller-facing policy enums are public at 1.0 with complete variant sets; a later variant costs a major.
Pruning ships at 1.0 via the migration policy; no separate log-rewrite entry point; compaction policy deferred and kept distinct from the permanent refusal in C3.2.
Migration is operator-initiated; pardosa never starts one. Stated at 1.0 without permanence across majors.
The named-constructor obligation extends to migration tooling as one rule rather than two.
The resume cursor is retained in the fixed surface, carries generation identity, and is rejected under its own name across a boundary.
Format/API split: metadata record shape fixed at 1.0, a narrow read-only operator interface answering three questions, everything else internal and unfixed.
Record-kind set fixed at 1.0 with unrecognised kinds rejected. The seven-then-nine enumeration by name is layer-10 artefact material and lands in a later slice.
An ownership record with no claim is unowned and claimable through the ordinary compare-and-set path.
The governing distinction stated once: a missing safety mechanism refuses, missing decision-cheapening evidence is indeterminate, and a platform lacking identity evidence remains a full writer.
Self-claim confined to the recursion base, so exactly one way exists to own any other artefact. Carried in the same clause as RULED 16, which states the base case.
Scope half only: wire shape and field encodings belong to the format specification. The operator-label design half is layer-6 and lands in a later slice.
Pair-movement requirement stated with its named failures; atomicity and tooling both refused.
Two split-brain directions, two names, and the read proceeding under either with no winner selected.
Takeover on proof only: a clean-release record proves release from any host, and the unproven residue is indeterminate and operator-initiated.
Superseded in direction by RULED 142, which reopened it: the top-level failure enumeration is complete and carries no open arm. C4.6 states the surviving position.
An indeterminate write outcome is its own outcome, folded into neither failure nor success, because the caller's next action differs.
Conformance asserts the promise and never the mechanism, so a stricter adapter conforms; every symmetric promise is an obligation.
Passing the published suite is what supporting a backend means, and a third party establishes conformance by running it.
The refusal line is drawn by what pardosa promises: refuse at open where a configuration breaks a promised invariant, document where the property is not promised.
The corruption guard is present in every build; no build option removes it. Stated as the property, with the dependency choice left to the implementation.
The adapter trait stays sealed at 1.0; a third party verifies conformance and does not ship an adapter. Opening the seal is an in-major addition, closing it a major change.
Type names and full public item paths are the surface; diagnostic string contents are data an operator reads.
Openness is designated by this specification rather than hand-maintained; C4.5 states the designation duty and records that no enumeration is designated open.
Lockstep release with sibling ranges rather than exact pins, so a consumer resolves one version of each pardosa crate.
The compiler floor stated as a rule rather than a number: oldest stable that compiles the fixed surface, a raise in any minor, no promised window. The current value is layer-12 constant material.
The two-regime promise, stated once as the axis every later marker is read against: invariants bind from 0.5.1, the surface is fixed at 1.0.
The format's reserved optional slot is bought and left unexposed; the consumer's own event type is the documented extension point.
Correlation deferred to W3C Trace Context; pardosa carries nothing natively and the spec states the deferral.
Published security policy with contact and process, no time commitment, direct monitoring of the non-Rust dependency edge, and withdrawal confined to correctness or safety defects.
The prohibition on contrastive definition governs this document's prose; its operative effect is the positive fiber definition C3.9 already carries. No clause instructs this document's authors.

Normative force lives in this specification alone; other published material orients, adds nothing, and carries no citation duty. Consistent with RULED 242, which withdrew the landing-page bar's clause status.

Superseded in direction by RULED 242: the landing-page bar carries no regime marker and is not a clause, so its enumeration's openness governs no clause. The bar survives, judged and recorded in the PAR ADR venue chosen at RULED 230, which is this effort's own record-keeping and not the library's behaviour. See escalation bead noted against RULED 90.

Superseded in direction by RULED 242, with the erratum owed under RULED 244 already filed on jn1.47: the documentation bar binds as a commitment but is not a clause and carries no marker. Its home is the PAR ADR corpus, which a library specification does not govern.

Per-clause axis marking, stated as the property. The two axes' names and binding dates are C4.1; the regime scheme's rules of operation are C5.1, added in sub-mission 04 as that row's own note anticipated, and are not restated in C4.2.

The marker's test and the standing rule that content mutability and regime are independent axes. OPEN ESCALATION pardosa-52d5: this ruling's landing-page application was superseded by RULED 242, and the sub-mission brief still directs the superseded reading; the standing rule itself survives and is what C4.2 carries.
Layout splits by axis: ordering and chaining bind from 0.5.1, byte arrangement is fixed at 1.0, and a layout clause must say which half it governs.

Ratified definition text carried verbatim. OPEN ESCALATION pardosa-8q05: its per-fiber narrowing was adopted to avoid pre-empting jn1.54, which has since contracted the total order in C3.8; not self-resolved.
Multi-dragline split is across artefacts; pardosa never partitions within one, and orders nothing between two.
One dragline per artefact converted from an implementation fact into a promise binding from 0.5.1.
No second dedicated envelope slot; an event never names its dragline. The slot already bought is the standing escape hatch.
The language rule applied as a refusal: a backend noun reaches no type, variant or path a consumer names. The replacement word for the routing parameter is layer-12 vocabulary material.
The metadata record's identity structure, multi-dragline-ready from 0.5.1: logical identity, version, member identifiers, partitioning rule.
One fiber in exactly one dragline, and therefore in exactly one artefact.

Cross-fiber order within a dragline holds between migrations as documented default behaviour, not as a contract; migrations may remove but not reorder. Depends on open escalation pardosa-8q05 over how far the dragline definition in C2.1 reaches; C4.17 takes the safest reading and states the order without widening C2.1.

The cross-fiber ordering refusal, sited as the opening clause of the titled refusal run inside the layer-5 section. Assumption named: the brief requires a citable refusal section and the section order is fixed by user instruction, so the run is a titled subsection rather than a tenth section. The refusal's scope is unchanged by the siting.
Reorder defined pairwise rather than sequence-wise, so one rule covers every migration policy and no taxonomy is needed.
Pairwise order preservation binds from 0.5.1 and the conformance suite asserts it. The invariant constrains pardosa where C5.40 constrains the consumer.
Order existence and replay determinism contracted; order content refused. See open escalation pardosa-8q05 against C2.1's narrower definition.
For a refusal clause the axis attaches to the refusal's force rather than to its deletion, stated so later refusal clauses inherit a rule.

Link integrity within a generation as the claim, with the three non-claims stated in the same clause. Sited in the refusal run, stating what pardosa establishes first and the refusals as consequences.
The two-tier frontier claim with the anchor gap named as a third value: unanchored is its own verdict rather than invalid, and tier two is an operator-elected capability.
Chain validation mandatory on every adapter and every reading path, with the invariant-breaking configuration inexpressible rather than defaulted off.
A discovered chain break refuses on every ordinary path under a third name beside refusal-for-missing-mechanism and indeterminate-for-missing-evidence; entry is an election named at the call site.
The per-artefact per-generation anchor obligation an operator satisfies is C5.29; the structural bar on any commitment spanning two artefacts is C5.43 in the refusal run.
The schema covers the payload type taken whole, variants included, and one type per artefact makes homogeneity a fact stated rather than a rule enforced.
Event kind is first-class pardosa vocabulary a stranger is taught, not merely a constraint on the payload type.
Naming the kinds that exist does not yield selection by kind; the refusal is stated where the new vocabulary makes the inference available.
Computed compatibility is a refusal without across-major permanence, with migration named as the positive substitute; C4.19 confines it to the 1.0 line.
The three statements bind from 0.5.1 as one clause family under one marker: always-refuse on a non-identical envelope shape, no computed compatibility, schema change is a migration.
The top-level failure enumeration is complete; the open-domain attribute is dropped. Reopens and replaces RULED 55.
Default polarity: public enumerations are complete unless this specification designates a named open domain.
The catch-all variant is refused; every variant names one condition. Closes the last route to growing the surface within a major.
The fiber's ordered same-fiber series is the enabling affordance, already promised; nothing further owed at 1.0.
Fixes whether PAR ADRs are living documents or immutable-plus-supersession. It governs this effort's own ADR corpus and record-keeping, not the library's behaviour.
A public struct's field set does not grow within a major line.
The in-major additive surface is closed at exactly three additions under one principle: the surface grows only by an addition a consumer cannot silently mis-handle.
The amended record set is re-fixed at 1.0 at nine kinds with the unrecognised-kind rejection unchanged. Enumeration by name deferred to the layer-10 artefact slice.
The five standard-owned envelope fields are fixed at 1.0, and the clause states that the format admits a sixth while the standard refuses one.
Tombstone read at migration only, keeping the no-query-surface refusal alive.
The five-module count is preserved by shedding material into the module whose concept already holds it. The internal crate rename is transfer-map construction and is not a 1.0 surface decision.
Artefacts are read only by the major line that wrote them; the operator links both majors and copies through. The technique is deliberately not taught here per RULED 235.
Envelope shape stays with this specification; the byte container's version belongs to the format specification. Never conflated.
The exclusion trait stays internal; the obligation is held by conformance rather than by the type system. Accepted cost: symmetry is tested, not structural.
The backend marker trait stays method-less and the two seals stay orthogonal, leaving a future backend nothing to break.
Homogeneity is the promise to a reader without the Rust types; C5.32 already states it and RULED 92 forbids a second statement of it.
The descriptor is mandatory in every artefact; the option to ship a self-undescribing artefact is closed.
Schema identity is a function of the descriptor; equality is the only comparison and version is the identity-differs relation and nothing more.
Identity is shape plus name, the consumer supplies the name, and the name is a component never a key; pardosa runs no registry.
Equality absolutely, and schema change is a migration. C4.19 already carries the always-refuse plus no-computed-compatibility family; no second clause is authored.
One word per concept, with the word schema owned by the payload type's identity and description.
The schema condition names the property rather than the detecting mechanism; the instance of the standing rule C5.55 states.
The comparison binds every event-yielding path on every adapter, and the suite asserts it, so symmetry is structural rather than incidental.
The payload type's root is an enumeration, each variant one event kind with a recorded discriminant; structures stay legal below the root.
Mandated variants are declared by the consumer and never injected; recognition is by pardosa's mark, not by the consumer's chosen name.
Judged spec-bearing rather than governance over this pass: the ruling governs every name in pardosa's own vocabulary, which is surface a stranger reads.

Refuses a PR-level decision-currency gate over this effort's own records. The ruling states its own class: a mechanism and process refusal changing nothing pardosa promises a stranger, and expressly not a citable refusal.
Fixes how closed bd tickets are read against the map body. The ruling states its own class: a record-keeping rule, not a spec clause.
Re-grounds the envelope identity value on the from-0.5.1 equality refusal that C4.19 carries. The ruling mints no clause of its own and preserves an outcome already stated.
Fixes that a non-substantive PAR ADR edit supersedes nothing. It governs this effort's ADR corpus and record-keeping, not the library's behaviour.
The obligation half survives as a property clause on how a public structure is constructed; the mechanism half is struck and stays unmandated.
The refuse-at-open tier is already carried by C5.35; the inexpressibility tier is design discipline governing how pardosa decides, and RULED 175 states it is not a spec clause.
Fixes when the RULED 173 design discipline fires. It governs a discipline that is itself not a spec clause, so it lands in none of its own.
States the existing refuse-at-open rule's reach as already covering consumer configuration; C5.35 states configuration unqualified and needs no widening.
Sets the PAR ADR edit-versus-supersede boundary. The ruling states its own class: a record-keeping rule, not a spec clause.
The scope-movement tie-breaker for PAR ADR supersession. Same class as RULED 177: record-keeping over the ADR corpus, not a spec clause.
Descriptor production is restricted to the published derive, with relaxation available as an addition within a major line.
The in-tree hand-written implementations are the named exception without which the derive-only restriction is false on its face.

Logical identity is operator-supplied, carries a generation boundary, and makes no tamper claim. ESCALATION OPEN: C5.20's sentence that no identity crosses the boundary reads wider than this exception; analysis in bd bead pardosa-de69, not self-resolved.
The partitioning rule is operator-declared and never inferred, and an uncovered fiber is a refusal at open rather than a default assignment.
Presence of the identity record is unconditional. C4.14 states the metadata record carries the identity structure with no absence case, so no second absence semantics is minted.
The record-yielding reader sits outside the schema comparison by design, and what it is given instead is the mandatory descriptor. Stated, not left inferable.
Purge acts on a tombstoned fiber under the purging migration policy alone; the link is made inside the existing policy set without minting a variant.
Exactly one mandated variant, the tombstone, and C5.51 states that set as complete at one.
Detach is refused and the refusal is recorded positively: the envelope already carries the fact, so no second durable rendering is required of a consumer.
Snapshot, migration record and correction are each refused as required kinds and recorded rather than left as silent absence.
Bounds what the citation sweep over this map's bd corpus may claim. It governs a tool over the corpus and reports nothing about pardosa's behaviour.
Fixes which agents the clean-room wall binds and where Notes-level rules reach. It governs the transfer map's charter, not the library's behaviour.
Rewrites contrastive charter entries positively. It governs the transfer map's charter text, not any statement a consumer of the library relies on.
Binds the map's own closing decision to an audited constraints list. It governs the map's closure and record-keeping, not the library's behaviour.

Records that a cyclic descriptor graph is refused by the language the consumer writes its payload type in, and that pardosa builds no mechanism of its own. There is no pardosa behaviour for a clause to state.
Ratifies a foreign governance corpus as advice this map may consult. It governs this map's citation practice, and the spec cites no foreign corpus normatively.
No ruling may rest solely on a foreign ADR. A citation-audit rule over this map's own record-keeping, with no library behaviour behind it.
Fixes that advice cannot overturn a ruling, with TigerStyle as the named instance. Precedence among this map's inputs, never a statement about pardosa.
Preserves record-without-a-gate where an ADR venue exists. It governs this effort's ADR corpus and review discipline, not the library's behaviour.
No release publishes a clause binding from 0.5.1 knowingly unmet, and the exclusion mechanism with its conformance assertion exists on every shipped adapter from the first published release.
The axis test is not widened to a quality judgement; C4.2 states the test unmodified, which is what this ruling preserves so no marked clause reopens.
